title: Saffron in Greenville Named South Carolina's Best Indian Restaurant Again
excerpt: FinanceBuzz and Yelp both point to the same Greenville dining room, while a newer national survey makes the case for Charleston's Rivayat.
body:
• Saffron Indian Cuisine in Greenville has been named South Carolina's best Indian restaurant in FinanceBuzz's state-by-state ranking, compiled from online reviews.
  • Yelp's best-in-every-state list reached the same verdict, citing a 4.5-star rating and diner praise for the authenticity of Saffron's cooking.
  • A newer 50-state survey from Tasting Table picked a different winner, Rivayat in Charleston, showing how fast the state's Indian dining scene is deepening.
  • Saffron is at 1178 Woodruff Road, #16, in Greenville and serves lunch and dinner, with its lunch service singled out for value.

Greenville is rarely the first South Carolina city mentioned for Indian food. Charleston usually takes that conversation. Yet when national publications rank the best Indian restaurant in every state, they keep landing on the same Woodruff Road dining room: Saffron Indian Cuisine.

Two rankings, one Greenville address

FinanceBuzz, which said it scoured online reviews to build its list of the top Indian restaurant in each state, named Saffron its South Carolina pick. The site described it as the best spot for anyone craving Indian food in the Greenville area, with a menu packed with the classics and lunch service that offers, in its words, some serious bargains for diners who come at midday.

Yelp's own state-by-state search, compiled from ratings and reviews and covered by 93.3 The Bus, reached the same conclusion. That coverage put Saffron at 4.5 out of 5 stars from more than 350 Yelp reviews, with diners praising the restaurant's authenticity. One reviewer called it "still the best Indian food I've had."

"Still the best Indian food I've had."

— Yelp reviewer, via 93.3 The Bus

The classics, done the familiar way

Saffron's appeal rests on the dishes that built Indian dining in America: curries, samosas, tikka masala and tandoori chicken, served across lunch and dinner. That is the North Indian canon — rich gravies, tandoor-cooked meats and breads — that became the default Indian menu in the United States over the past four decades.

Tasting Table, introducing its own 50-state survey, acknowledged that skew directly. Butter chicken reigns supreme in America, it noted, largely because Indian restaurateurs have had to cater to local taste buds to make a living, and North Indian dishes dominate lists like these as a result. Saffron's repeated selection is, in that sense, a verdict on execution: the familiar repertoire, cooked well enough and consistently enough to top the state.

A newer challenger in Charleston

The consensus is not unanimous, and the disagreement is instructive. Tasting Table's survey, published in September and curated from online customer reviews, local press and awards, chose Rivayat in Charleston for South Carolina. It pointed readers to creative cooking — a burrata saag alongside a familiar chana masala — and to a bar program that won a 2026 award for Charleston's best espresso martini, made with a spicy Indian twist. Rivayat, at 210 Rutledge Avenue, represents the newer, chef-driven end of the state's Indian scene.

Two methodologies produce two winners. Review-based rankings reward a Greenville institution that has pleased a broad local audience for years. A curatorial list rewards a Charleston newcomer pushing the cuisine in new directions. Both can be true at once, and together they describe a state whose Indian dining is no longer a single story.

What it means for diaspora diners

For Indian families in the Upstate, the ranking confirms something more practical than bragging rights: a dependable kitchen for the dishes of home, close enough for a weeknight. Restaurants like Saffron function as community infrastructure as much as businesses — the place for a family celebration, or for introducing colleagues to Indian food for the first time.

The Charleston alternative matters for the same reason. A creative Indian kitchen winning national attention in the Lowcountry signals that South Carolina diners, diaspora and otherwise, are ready for regional range beyond the standard menu.

What to watch

State-by-state rankings refresh regularly, and Rivayat's rising profile gives Saffron a credible challenger for the next round. For now, the review-based verdict stands: readers heading to Greenville can test it at 1178 Woodruff Road, and readers in Charleston can compare it with the city's newest contender on Rutledge Avenue.
